site.title: Hari Kampo
site.tagline: A kampo pharmacy: herbs weighed by hand, one person at a time.

categories.name: Seasons
categories.description: Eating and living with the season.

categories.name: Herbs
categories.description: Single herbs from the drawer wall.

posts.title: Autumn dryness and pears
posts.excerpt: Dry throat, dry skin, a cough that starts in October: what we weigh most this month.
posts.content:
Kampo calls autumn the dry season. The cough that arrives with the first cold mornings is dry and tickly, and the skin on the hands cracks.

We weigh more ophiopogon and lily bulb this month. At home, a pear steamed with a little honey does the same work, more slowly.

posts.title: How a formula is weighed
posts.excerpt: Fourteen packets, eight herbs each, weighed to a tenth of a gram.
posts.content:
A two-week decoction is fourteen paper packets. Each herb is weighed for all fourteen at once, then split by eye and checked on the scale.

It takes about twenty minutes. Most people wait at the counter with a cup of barley tea.

posts.title: Four herbs we open every day
posts.excerpt: Ginseng, licorice, cinnamon bark and jujube: the drawers that are never full.
posts.content:
Of two hundred drawers, four are refilled every week. Licorice is in most formulas; jujube and ginger travel together.

Ginseng is the expensive one. We buy it whole and slice it on the counter.

posts.title: The drawer wall
posts.excerpt: Two hundred drawers, each with a name brushed on paper.
posts.content:
The hyakumi-dansu came from a pharmacy in Osaka that closed in 1931. Each drawer has two compartments, so the wall holds four hundred herbs at most.

The names are brushed on paper labels and replaced when they fade, about once every ten years.
